n: With construction complete, Solomon placed in the temple treasury all the silver, gold, and vessels David had dedicated. Father and son together brought the house to completion.

f.w: the things that David his father had dedicated

n: Solomon gathered the leaders of every tribe to bring the ark up from the City of David — the old Jebusite stronghold of Zion — to the new temple on the higher hill to the north.

f.w: the city of David, which is Zion

n: The dedication took place during the feast of the seventh month — the Feast of Tabernacles, Israel’s joyful harvest festival.

f.w: the feast which was in the seventh month
f.g: The Feast of Tabernacles (Booths), in the month Ethanim/Tishri.

n: This time the ark was carried properly by the Levites, as the law required — unlike the earlier attempt with a cart that ended in Uzza’s death.

f.w: the Levites took up the ark

n: The ark, the old tabernacle tent from Gibeon, and its holy vessels were all brought up together, uniting Israel’s worship in one place.
As the procession moved, the king and people offered so many sheep and cattle that no one could count them — overflowing gratitude.
The priests set the ark in its permanent home: the innermost room, beneath the outstretched wings of the great cherubim.

f.g: The inner sanctuary, the most holy place.

n: The cherubim’s wings formed a canopy over the ark and its carrying poles.

f.g: The carrying poles of the ark.

n: The poles were drawn forward so their ends could be seen from just outside the inner room, but not from farther away. “Unto this day” shows the Chronicler is copying an older source written while the temple still stood.
Only the two stone tablets of the Ten Commandments were inside the ark. At the heart of the temple was God’s covenant word.
All the priests present had purified themselves for this event and served together, not by their usual rotating shifts.

f.w: did not then wait by course
f.g: Did not keep to their normal assigned divisions.

n: Levite singers from the families of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, dressed in white linen, played cymbals, lyres, and harps beside 120 priests blowing trumpets.

f.g: Stringed instruments like lyres or harps.

n: When musicians and singers praised in perfect unity — “For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever” — the cloud of God’s presence filled the house. Unity in worship invites God’s presence.

f.w: For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever

n: The glory was so overwhelming that the priests could not continue their service. Just as at the tabernacle’s dedication, God accepted this house as His own. Latter-day Saints recall similar outpourings at the Kirtland Temple dedication.

f.w: the glory of the LORD had filled the house
